newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Giscard sees 2.7 pct growth due to franc.
newsitem.headline: France's Giscard sees 2.7 pct growth due to franc.

text.p: Former French President Valery Giscard d'Estaing, who sparked a brief debate last year about the need for the French franc to depreciate, said on Wednesday the currency was now at a better level against the dollar.
He also believed the level of the franc after the dollar's recent rise could, if it lasted, add a half a percentage point to GDP growth in 1997, bringing it to around 2.7 percent.
"Today it's at 5.55 (against the dollar), we're now in the zone we wanted," Giscard d'Estaing said on LCI television.
"We should stay in this zone...it could give us an extra 0.5 percent of GDP and that means around 2.7 percent (GDP growth) this year," he said, adding that this should help to promote job creation.
Giscard called for more cuts in official interest rates.
"Our monetary policy still has room for manoeuvre," he said. The franc was at 5.5590/10 versus the dollar on Wednesday evening.

Giscard touched a raw nerve in France last year when he first spoke of the need for a depreciated franc to help growth and jobs at a time when France -- as it still does -- faced record 12.7 percent unemployement.
